T: Lowell's own. Pull up a stool.
D: A working-class boxer from Lowell, Massachusetts tries to escape the shadow of his troubled brother.
P: Serve the mains when Micky takes Charlene out after her shift at the bar.
S: Beer-battered onion rings with malt aioli
Thick onion rings in crisp lager batter, malt aioli for dipping

Thick onion rings dipped in a cold lager batter and fried golden and crisp, salted hot and served with a malt vinegar and garlic aioli. Cut 2 large brown onions into 1cm rings and separate. Whisk 150g plain flour, 1 tsp baking powder and a pinch of salt with 250ml cold lager until just smooth. Dust the rings in flour, dip in the batter and fry in batches at 180C for 2 to 3 minutes until golden. Salt straight away. Mix 150g mayonnaise with 1 tbsp malt vinegar and a crushed garlic clove for the dip.
Thin-sliced roast beef, barbecue mayo and American cheese on slider buns
Beef topside roasted rare, sliced paper thin, piled into soft rolls with a tangy barbecue sauce, mayo and white American cheese.

Bacon rendered, onion, celery and potato softened, clam juice and milk added, clams and cream at the end, served in small cups with oyster crackers. Fry 150g diced bacon until crisp. Add a diced onion and 2 celery sticks and soften 5 minutes. Stir in 2 tbsp flour, then 2 cans baby clams with their juice drained into 300ml, plus 300ml milk and 2 diced potatoes. Simmer 15 minutes until the potato is tender. Add the clams and 150ml cream and heat through without boiling. Season with pepper and serve in cups with oyster crackers and chives.
M: Alice's Sunday pot roast and gravy
the loud house full of sisters

Beef chuck seared dark and braised with onion, carrot, celery, red wine and thyme until fork tender, with potatoes cooked in the juices and a thick gravy. Season a 1.5kg beef chuck roast and sear on all sides in a heavy casserole. Add 2 quartered onions, 3 carrots, 2 celery sticks, 250ml red wine, 500ml beef stock and thyme. Cover and braise at 160C for 2 hours. Add 800g halved potatoes and cook 1 hour more. Lift out the meat and veg, then simmer the liquid with 1 tbsp cornflour mixed in water until thick. Slice and serve with the gravy.
Ziti baked in Italian sausage tomato sauce with melted cheese

Ziti tossed in a fennel sausage and tomato sauce with dollops of ricotta, baked under a bubbling mozzarella and parmesan crust. Squeeze 400g Italian sausages from their skins and brown in a pan, breaking them up. Add 2 crushed garlic cloves, 700g passata and a pinch of chilli flakes and simmer 15 minutes. Boil 500g ziti or penne for 2 minutes less than the packet says. Toss with the sauce, spread in a baking dish and dot with 250g ricotta. Top with 200g grated mozzarella and 40g parmesan and bake at 200C for 25 minutes.
W: Sponge layers filled with vanilla custard under chocolate glaze
Two vanilla sponges baked at 175C, sandwiched with chilled vanilla pastry cream, topped with dark chocolate ganache poured over and left to set.
K: Pale ale topped with Irish stout poured over the back of a spoon

A pint of cold pale ale with Irish stout poured slowly over the back of a spoon so it sits in a dark layer on top. Chill four pint glasses in the freezer for 15 minutes. Pour a 375ml can of pale ale into each glass, tilting it so the head stays small. Hold a spoon upside down just above the beer and slowly pour 200ml Irish stout over the back of it so it floats in a dark layer on top. Serve straight away before the layers mix.
